summary: The Bipartisan IVF for Military Families Act amends title 10 of the United States Code to provide fertility-related care, including in vitro fertilization (IVF), under the TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select programs for active duty members of the Armed Forces and their dependents. It sets specific rules for treatments, limits, prohibitions, and care coordination starting October 1, 2027.

affected_groups.effect: Receive coverage for fertility-related care and treatments like IVF, egg retrieval, sperm retrieval, and preservation under TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select without specific waiting periods after an infertility diagnosis.
affected_groups.group: Active duty members of the Armed Forces and their dependents

affected_groups.effect: Are explicitly excluded from receiving these specific fertility-related care benefits under TRICARE contracts.
affected_groups.group: Former members of the Armed Forces and their dependents

affected_groups.effect: Receive training and support from the Secretary of Defense regarding the unique needs of military members and their dependents under the care coordination program.

key_provisions: Requires fertility-related care to be covered under TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select for active duty service members and their dependents.
Allows up to three completed oocyte retrievals per calendar year for in vitro fertilization treatments, with single embryo transfers provided unless medically indicated otherwise.
Prohibits cost-sharing penalties specifically for fertility-related care and bans waiting periods or extra limitations once an individual is diagnosed with infertility.
Bans Department of Defense funds from being used for preimplantation genetic screening, human cloning, international surrogacy, or artificial womb technology.

Establishes a fertility-related care coordination program by the Secretary of Defense to ensure timely care and provide training and support to community health care providers regarding the unique needs of military members and their dependents.
Applies the new fertility care amendments to services provided on or after October 1, 2027.
missing_information: Specific cost estimates or funding amounts required to implement the TRICARE fertility treatment program.
Detailed descriptions of how the Department of Defense will measure or enforce provider training standards.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Bipartisan IVF for Military Families Act amends title 10 of the United States Code to provide fertility-related care, including in vitro fertilization (IVF), under the TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select programs for active duty members of the Armed Forces and their dependents. It sets specific rules for treatments, limits, prohibitions, and care coordination starting October 1, 2027.
summary_detail.significance: This bill alters military health benefits by introducing comprehensive fertility treatment and IVF coverage into the TRICARE program for active duty families starting in late 2027, while explicitly prohibiting certain advanced genetic and reproductive technologies.
